opportunity: RE-need function-inventory-silently-lists — `kuna functions` on a NEOLite-packed PE returned six zero-sized import entries, exit 0, error null, while `kuna decompile-all` on the same file named the cause and exited 1 (crackmes.one 5ab77f5433c5d40ad448c1c1 bin/CryptoME.zip.__x/CryptoME.exe, round 12).
test_name: kuna functions / --summary zero-discovery verdict, witness + 940-binary dataset sweep + 250 /usr/bin ELFs
decisions: The refuter's diagnosis is UPHELD and reproduced verbatim: the diagnostic is already wired into `run_functions`, and `all.is_empty()` is false because the six import pointer slots are inventory entries. Both duplicated sites (run_functions at decompile_all.rs:1120 and run_summary at :1178) are fixed; `--summary` had the identical hole.

The predicate is NOT the refuter's suggested `size > 0`. On this class of image the funcextent clip returns 0 for every entry (no section publishes a CODE span and a PE has no load segments to fall back on), so a size test would fire on an image whose bodies were all discovered and would be a second guess about what a body is. The right predicate already exists and is the one `decompile-all` reads its own verdict off: `function_entries_executable`, which excludes an entry on the loader's own import_slot_ranges knowledge rather than on a flag. Aligning `functions` to it makes the three surfaces one answer by construction instead of by coincidence.

`ConsoleProgram::any_executable_entry` is added rather than calling `function_entries_executable().is_empty()`, which would re-run the canonical enumeration a second time on a surface that already holds it (274k-function images exist). One section-table walk, no second enumeration; a cargo test asserts the cheap answer equals the expensive one on five fixtures.

NO new option, NO phases.toml/options.rs/catalog/DIV/docs/options.md edits and NO tests/stages XML — tooling track. A CLI verdict predicate cannot change emitted C, and the stages corpus loads <bytechunk> images through LoadImageXml, which never constructs the ObjectLoadImage a PE import table needs.

The exit code moves 0 -> 1 with the error, automatically: emit_with_discovery_error returns i32::from(discovery_error.is_some()). That is the established contract, already pinned by the promoted probe tests/cli/zero-functions-exit-0.json, not a new decision.

The witness's six import names are correct output and are preserved: count stays 6 with all six names, and the promoted probe pins count AND the names AND the error, so it cannot go green on a run that simply lists nothing.

SCOPE LIMIT, recorded because the acceptance depends on it: this need is only correct while bare discovery finds nothing in the packed image. `kuna functions BIN --define-function 0x4f7001-0x4f700c=entry` already answers count 7, error null, and still does. If discovery ever reaches into .NEOpack on its own, close this by supersession rather than reading the red acceptance as a regression.
